lines: Gosha Town, the hidden village of the Taimanin.
A town that ordinary people could never even approach, yet for some reason, it has been seeing a surge of unusual visitors lately.
Residents from parallel worlds just a little while in the past, inhabitants of entirely different worlds, or conversely, visitors from the future.
Sometimes we welcome such guests, but other times we get dragged into the commotion they cause and are left scrambling to deal with it.
Some might say that problems only arise because we get involved, but if you ask me, that is not the case.
It was precisely because we engaged with them proactively that we were able to guide the issues to a resolution before they became critical.
As a result, it had become common sense in Gosha to involve ourselves with guests as much as possible.
That said...
Me
(Not from the recent past, not from the future, and not from a completely different world either...)
To put it bluntly, a figure whose very existence cannot be confirmed, from a time so remote it is shrouded in secrecy...
That was the unusual guest this time.
Oboro
I am truly sorry... for a woman of such dubious origins, to have you guide me through the town.
A woman walking beside me, wearing a kimono with a hood pulled over her head to keep a low profile. Her name was Oboro.
However, she was not the famous Oboro of the underworld, but a completely different person who claimed to be a ninja from Iga.
Me
It is nothing. I am quite used to this sort of thing.
It seemed that in Gosha, or at least in the mind of Sensei Igawa Asagi, handling and entertaining such guests was something that would work out fine if left to me.
Still, in this particular case, it might be a natural progression for the task to fall to me—or rather, to the Fuuma clan.
Our guest this time, Oboro of Iga.
It appeared that her eyes held a power capable of breaking through any ninja technique—nullifying its effects.
In other words, it was a kind of Demon Eye that manifested in our clan.
Me
(Nullifying the effects of any technique... I feel like I have heard that story somewhere before.)
But setting that aside for now.
Me
For now, regarding Oboro-san's situation, we are planning to have her stay with Gosha and my family while we look for a way to send her back.
Oboro
Yes, thank you very much... And I am grateful for your hospitality.
As we walked through the town discussing the plan, she stopped for a moment and bowed deeply.
As the granddaughter of the clan leader, she should have been arrogant, but she was surprisingly humble.
Me
Well, please don't be so formal. Since this is a town of only ninjas, please feel at home.
Oboro
Y-Yes... I am truly sorry for the trouble... But...
As she spoke, she lifted the hem of her kimono slightly, glanced around, and widened her eyes.
Oboro
I am ignorant of the world to begin with... But even so, everything is different from my time...
Indeed.
Being told to relax in such a town would be difficult, as she would be curious about everything.
Me
I believe it was the Keicho era... Compared to over three hundred years ago, it is only natural that you do not understand much.
That is right—she lived during the Tokugawa era, the Edo period.
Gosha's streets have a certain antiquity, with traces of the Showa era visible everywhere, but even Showa is a distant future from the Edo period.
Thrown into such a future world alone, she is amazing just for being able to converse normally with people from the future.
Me
If there is anything you are curious about, please do not hesitate to ask.
Oboro
T-Then... What are these stone pillars?
What caught her eye as we walked were the utility poles erected all over the town.
Me
These are called utility poles. They are used to transmit electricity, telegraph signals, or both, to houses and buildings.
Oboro
Denryoku... and denshin?
Hiraga Gennai repaired the Eirekiteru, if I recall correctly, during the An'ei era.
That was over a hundred years after Keicho, so there could be no concept of electricity.
So naturally, I intended to add an explanation for that as well.
Me
Electricity is like fuel or power, the thing needed to make any mechanism run.
I found the concepts of fuel and power tricky, too, since I wasn't sure when they started being used.
I did add a brief note, using firewood and charcoal as examples of fuel, and human labor as an example of power.
Me
As for the mechanisms themselves, we call them machines. Most machines run on electricity, and I suspect they handle the bulk of household chores.
For instance, I mentioned the washing machine, the most mechanized of the home appliances.
Me
You put the laundry in the machine and leave it to its own devices, and it washes, wrings, and in some cases, even dries the clothes for you.
Oboro
W-What a convenience... Does that mean they dry fine no matter how many days it rains?
Me
That is the case with washer-dryers. Even without them, you can use heating to dry clothes indoors.
I explained heating again as a developed and evolved version of the irori or fire brazier.
I explained the mechanics as best I could, but even a modern person would likely find it hard to understand.
Oboro seemed to have gone beyond the limits of her comprehension, standing there frozen in a daze.
Me
There are also refrigerators and freezers, storage rooms like a himuro, that can be used in ordinary homes regardless of the season.
Oboro
A himuro! Anytime!
The content that made me burst into laughter seemed to snap Oboro out of her freeze, and she looked even more astonished.
Oboro
T-Those aren't ninja arts, are they...
Me
Using the electricity sent through the power lines connected to this utility pole, ordinary people can use them just like anyone else.
You can live comfortably without any special powers.
That is what the development of science is all about.
Other problems may arise, but if you trade them for convenience and comfort, it would be hard to give up this way of life.
Me
It's mostly the same with lighting at night. If you operate the switch, a room can be lit up as bright as midday in an instant.
As I spoke, I casually shone my phone's flashlight into the narrow alleyway hidden in the shadow of the building we had just passed.
Me
In place of lanterns, we have lights that can illuminate dark places. And it's not just this one; there are several different types.
Oboro
...I am constantly surprised... I do not know what to say... I am at a loss for words...
It is easy to say "the future," but this is practically another world.
While stories about bringing modern science to medieval civilizations are well-known in other-world fiction, if the roles were reversed, this would be the expected reaction.
Me
(Well, there are plenty of stories like that too... like people from the past coming to the modern era.)
Setting that aside.
Me
That covers electricity. Next is the telegraph. This is a communication network that uses electrical signals.
Oboro
Communication... do you mean letters?
Me
Exactly.
Looking up at the power lines, she might be imagining baskets filled with letters being sent along the wires to distant places.
Me
Letters still exist, but they are delivered by people. Well, not on foot, but by car.
Regarding cars, I explained that while some use electricity, others run on a different fuel, pointing to a car driving down the road.
Oboro
Oh, so letters are carried by those... Are the letters transported by such means reserved for the nobility?
Me
No, ordinary people use them too. However, there is easier communication than letters, so they are not used as much anymore.
Oboro
Letters... are no longer used...
She looked shocked. Perhaps she had a deep attachment to letters.
As the daughter of a clan leader, she might have had a fiancé or a lover...
If she had exchanged letters with such a person, she must have loved the romance of it.
Me
Um... well, with easier communication, you can feel like you are always with the other person.
Oboro
Always with that person!
She latched onto that idea with great enthusiasm.
Oboro
I-I'm sorry... that... that is a good thing in its own right...
To cover her slip, she cleared her throat with a cough, and her gaze drifted toward the power lines, then up to the sky.
Oboro
As for how we used to deliver letters, we used hawks.
Me
Carrier hawks?
I heard that using pigeons relies on their homing instinct, but training hawks must require quite a bit of effort.
However, since hawks are also highly combat-capable, they offer the advantage of not being limited to mere transport.
Me
No, wait. Maybe it isn't training, but a technique to control animals...
The words slipped out before I could stop them, and upon hearing them, Oboro's lips curled into a faint smile.
Oboro
If that were the case, the hawks would stop obeying me the moment they saw my eyes.
Me
Ah... right, that's true.
The Demon Eye that nullifies all ninja arts...
It forcibly drags the opponent into a stage of physical ability and swordsmanship, or perhaps martial arts. It is truly an eye that kills ninjas.
Moreover, from the enemy's perspective, only they are burdened with that handicap, while being attacked one-sidedly by techniques.
If Oboro did not have such a kind and gentle personality, she would never have been allowed to go out freely, even in Gosha, which is known for its moderate faction.
Oboro
So, what exactly is this telegraph you mentioned?
Hearing Oboro's question, I snapped back to reality.
Me
It's the electrical communication I mentioned earlier. You can send text instantly, or hold a conversation with someone far away as if they were right there.
I explained that the forms vary, and once again, Oboro's eyes widened.
Oboro
So... that means we can exchange messages without having to deliver letters...
Me
That is exactly what it means.
Oboro
In that case... it might be inevitable that letters will fade away...
Oboro muttered with a hint of melancholy, but it seemed she was struggling internally, thinking that if such a convenient thing existed, she should accept it.
Oboro
And this other part... being able to converse with people far away?
Me
That is exactly how it works. For example... using a machine like this to reproduce the voice, you might say.
It receives sound waves as a signal, transmits them via radio waves, and reproduces the signal at the destination to deliver the same sound to a distant location.
As for the principle of the telephone, broadly speaking, that is the gist of it.
Oboro
On... on such a small board...
I showed her the smartphone and explained. She gazed at it with curiosity, picked it up, and seemed slightly surprised by its texture.
Oboro
And this is possible instantly?
Me
Yes. I hear it used to take time and the audio quality was poor, but nowadays it is no different from talking to someone right next to you.
Oboro
That is... how enviable...
I wondered who she was imagining. A faint flush of red seemed to appear on her face, hidden by her haori.
Oboro
But then again... it makes me feel restless that I cannot meet them... If I could hear their voice, I would surely want to touch them.
Me
Touching is difficult... Since you can see their face while talking, it probably makes it even more frustrating.
Oboro
Seeing their face!
Apparently, that feature has its own demand.
Oboro
Nngh... yes, that would be wonderful... If I could always see that person's face and talk to them...
Hearing this kind of talk, the first thing I imagined was an affair, which is also proof of her gentle nature.
An ordinary ninja hearing this would first think about how much their work would be facilitated.
Of course for espionage, but also as a means of communication on the battlefield, it would undoubtedly be invaluable.
In fact, even mobile phones, which were initially very large, became the first tools used on the battlefield.
Me
(She really has no such thoughts at all... she is a good person...)
It is the same with roads.
In the early Edo period, right after the Sengoku era ended, memories of battles would still be fresh.
Roads in that era were likely left rough and steep paths untouched to make it difficult for enemies to attack.
Even the roads Nobunaga had built up were likely just leveled dirt or sand, with ditches dug along the edges.
Asphalt paving would have been unknown to them, and the sight of such clean roads stretching out wide and long would have been a complete culture shock.
When she first saw such roads, she had widened her eyes in awe, praising them as amazing.
Oboro
This is... if I understood the mechanism, could I make one...?
I was just thinking that when, out of the blue, I heard such an out-of-left-field question and was startled.
However, she did not seem interested in using it for ninja purposes, but rather focused solely on it as a tool for making phone calls with someone.
Me
...It would be difficult for you to do it alone. Even if you fully understood the mechanism, it would require advanced technology...
It would not be possible to reproduce it in the Edo period unless dozens or hundreds of people with the same level of technical skill and knowledge gathered to develop it.
Oboro
I see...
Me
I'm sorry, I couldn't be of more help.
Oboro
No! No, that's not it! I'm the one who is being strange--Kyah!
In her haste to explain herself, she tripped over her feet, likely due to the unfamiliar paved road, and nearly fell.
Me
Gh... Oboro-san!
I caught her just in time, so she did not get hurt--probably.
Me
Can you stand? Did you twist your ankle or anything...
Oboro
Y-yes, I am fine... I am sorry, for showing you such an embarrassing side.
Still holding my hand for support, she checked her foot and lowered her head shyly.
Oboro
Even though I am a ninja, I fall over like this often... I am immature and pathetic.
Me
No, please don't worry about it at all. People trip, even ninjas trip normally, and if anything, I trip sometimes too.
Oboro
Hearing you say that... thank you for your concern.
I let go of her hand, but she had no particular injuries and seemed able to walk normally.
Me
With that outfit... I mean, those sandals, they seem more likely to get caught on sandy ground. It's different from regular cobblestones, after all.
Oboro
Haa... when you put it that way, it seems like there aren't many people around who dress like me.
It's not that there are no women in traditional Japanese attire, but there are only a handful.
In modern times, most people wear Western-style clothing.
Me
Since we don't know how long we'll be staying, if we want to avoid drawing attention here, it might be a good idea to procure some Western-style clothes.
I pointed at a few girls walking through town in that kind of attire, and she stared at them intently before eventually letting out a sigh.
Oboro
I think they are lovely outfits, but... I don't have the means to have something like that tailored...
Me
Tailored... Ah, right.
Clothes in that era were basically second-hand, and commoners would repair a single garment repeatedly to wear it for a long time.
New clothes were mostly custom-made, which was also a privilege of the wealthy class.
Naturally, as the daughter of the head of the ninja clan, her kimono was likely custom-tailored.
Me
In modern times, manufacturing technology has advanced, so those kinds of clothes are mass-produced and anyone can buy them easily.
However, unlike custom-made items, issues with fit and comfort are unavoidable.
Me
Just buying them wouldn't cost that much, and it seems the Taimanin organization can advance us some living expenses.
Of course, it's not entirely up to me; Fuuma Tokiko holds the purse strings for expenses.
Oboro
Clothes with such intricate designs, in such large quantities... I am simply amazed...
Perhaps the sigh she let out was because she was imagining herself wearing Western-style clothing.
As we walked, Oboro watched the clothes of the people we passed, gazing after them with delight several times, but eventually, she smiled with a hint of loneliness.
Oboro
But, I wonder if they would suit me... As someone who is relying on your kindness, I cannot ask for such a waste of money.
Given her personality, that is what she would say.
Still, there was plenty of room to push back.
Me
It is different from your usual attire, so I can understand why you might feel a sense of discomfort based on your own imagination.
Oboro
I, I suppose so?
Me
However, objectively speaking, it is rude of me to say, but a beautiful woman like you, Oboro, would likely pull off modern clothing without any awkwardness.
Oboro
W-What are you saying... Do not joke like that...!
Modern ninjas, including in their fashion sense, are often bright about entertainment and actively enjoy it.
But in the Edo period, when the era of the serious ninja was at its peak, they probably had no leisure to enjoy such things.
If I were to let her return after she had tasted the flavors of modern culture, it might cause complications in her subsequent life in the Edo period.
Me
I just want her to let her hair down a bit and have some fun...
I made it clear that, at least from my perspective, the question of whether it suits her or not was not an issue.
The remaining problem was the cost.
Me
Also, regarding clothes, it is important. It would be a problem if you wore the same thing every day, so you would need to change...
Me
In modern times, kimonos are not mass-produced. They need to be tailored, which makes them even more expensive.
Oboro
I see... Is that really true?
Me
You can ask at a kimono shop if you like. Well, in that case, mass-produced Western-style clothing ends up being the cheaper option.
Oboro
I, I see... If that is the case, then it is... unavoidable... I suppose...?
As a woman of her age, she must be interested in flashy clothes too.
Smiling at Oboro, who was struggling with that conflict, I realized we had come near a certain shop.
Me
Well, let us think about the clothes later. We have been walking this whole time, so how about having something sweet nearby?
Oboro
Sweet... Could it be... sugar?!
Ah, right. Sugar was a luxury item in the Edo period, wasn't it?
Me
It is an even more intense sweetness. This is also an affordable price in modern times.
Oboro
Sweet things, at an affordable price...!
I couldn't bring myself to act spoiled, yet I simply couldn't give up on sweets.
Just as she was caught in that internal struggle, a cute gurgle echoed from her stomach.
Me
You look tired, so let's head out.
Oboro
Yes... I am so embarrassed...
Pressing her hand to her stomach as if to scold it, she bowed her head, her face flushed red, and nodded in response.
